paragraphs: Build terrariums and watch them live. A mechanistic simulation of closed, bioactive terrariums (water cycle, gas exchange, plants, clean-up crew, mold and pests) with a web interface for designing jars and keeping a shelf of them.
Nothing is scripted. The first-month mold bloom, the springtail boom and crash, fittonia fainting, the sunny-windowsill death spiral: all of it falls out of the rules in src/engine.
features: Shelf: every terrarium as a living jar on a shelf, with a tag showing its day, health and most pressing issue. A compare table for tracking several at once, and a "since you last looked" summary.
Builder: six steps (vessel, layers, plants, clean-up crew, placement, name) starting from a recipe or blank, with a live preview, inline warnings, and a 90-day forecast that reruns as you design.
Jar view: conditions, issues with one-tap fixes, care actions (mist, air out, feed, remove mold, prune, change lid or placement), plant and animal rosters, trends and a journal.
Time: paused, real time (jars keep living while you are away), a day per second, or a week per second.

Handle the jar: drag to spin it; flick it and it rocks on its base and settles, with the plants swaying. Tap a plant for its name and health, tap the soil to startle the animals (springtails hop, isopods run, pill bugs…

requirements.text: Community shelf: pick a username (no email or password: you get a recovery code to sign in elsewhere) and share jars you are proud of.
Anyone can browse, like and plant a copy without an account.
